author: Vitor
aiExplanation: This function counts how many servers in a grid can **communicate** with at least one other server, where a server (a cell equal to `1`) can talk to any other server sharing its row or column. It first makes two tally arrays, `rows` and `cols`, and does one pass over the grid so that `rows[i]` holds how many servers sit in row `i` and `cols[j]` holds how many sit in column `j`. Then it does a second pass: for every cell that is a server, it checks whether its row **or** its column contains more than one server (`rows[i] > 1 || cols[j] > 1`); if so, that server is not isolated and `count` goes up by one. The final `count` is returned. Because each pass touches every cell once, the whole thing runs in **O(m × n)** time with **O(m + n)** extra space for the two tally arrays.

aiExplanation: The function `countServers` figures out how many servers (cells holding a `1`) in a 2D `grid` are **connected** to at least one other server, where two servers are connected if they share a row or a column. It starts by building two counters, `rows` (one slot per row) and `cols` (one slot per column), and walks the grid once, bumping `rows[i]` and `cols[j]` each time it finds a server. On a second walk it looks at every server again and asks: does my row have more than one server, **or** does my column? If either is true (`rows[i] > 1 || cols[j] > 1`), the server can communicate, so `res` is incremented. The function returns `res`, the total number of communicating servers. Both passes visit each cell exactly once, giving **O(m × n)** time, and the two counter arrays use only **O(m + n)** extra memory.
